EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK AND WORKPLACE
POLICIES
Northwind Technologies Ltd.
Document Version: 3.2 | Effective: January 1, 2026
Classification: Internal Use | Policy ID: HR-POL-2026-001
Effective Date: January 1, 2026
This handbook supersedes all previous versions. Employees must
acknowledge receipt within 30 days.
SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION AND EMPLOYMENT
RELATIONSHIP
1.1 Purpose. This Employee Handbook establishes the policies, procedures,
and expectations that govern the employment relationship between Northwind
Technologies Ltd. ("Company") and its employees. These policies apply to all
full-time, part-time, and temporary employees unless otherwise specified.

1.2 At-Will Employment. Employment with the Company is "at-will,"
meaning either the employee or the Company may terminate the employment
relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice. Nothing in this
handbook creates a contract of employment or guarantees employment for any
specific duration.
1.3 Equal Employment Opportunity. The Company is committed to
providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants
without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability,
genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any
other characteristic protected by applicable law.
Definition - Employee Classifications:
Full-Time: Employees regularly scheduled for 30+ hours per week.

other characteristic protected by applicable law.
Definition - Employee Classifications:
Full-Time: Employees regularly scheduled for 30+ hours per week.
Part-Time: Employees regularly scheduled for fewer than 30 hours per
week.
Temporary: Employees hired for a specific project or limited duration.
Page 1

SECTION 2: COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS
2.1 Pay Periods and Methods
Employees are paid bi-weekly on alternate Fridays. If a payday falls on a
holiday, payment will be issued on the preceding business day. All employees
must enroll in direct deposit within 30 days of hire. Pay statements are
available through the employee self-service portal.
2.2 Overtime Compensation
Non-exempt employees are entitled to overtime pay at 1.5 times their regular
hourly rate for all hours worked exceeding 40 in a workweek. Overtime must
be pre-approved by the employee's supervisor. Unauthorized overtime may
result in disciplinary action, though all hours worked will be compensated.
Important: Exempt employees are not eligible for overtime
compensation. Classification as exempt or non-exempt is determined

Important: Exempt employees are not eligible for overtime
compensation. Classification as exempt or non-exempt is determined
based on job duties and salary level in accordance with the Fair Labor
Standards Act (FLSA).
2.3 Health Insurance Benefits
Full-time employees are eligible for health insurance benefits on the first day of
the month following 60 days of employment. The Company offers medical,

dental, and vision coverage options. The Company contributes 80% of the
premium cost for employee-only coverage and 60% for dependent coverage.
2.4 Retirement Benefits
The Company offers a 401(k) retirement savings plan to all employees who
have completed 90 days of service. The Company provides a matching
contribution of 100% of the first 3% of salary deferred, plus 50% of the next
2% deferred (maximum match of 4%). Employees are immediately vested in
their own contributions; Company matching contributions vest over a 3-year
period.
Page 2

SECTION 3: TIME OFF AND LEAVE POLICIES
3.1 Paid Time Off (PTO)
Full-time employees accrue PTO based on length of service according to the
following schedule:
0-2 years of service: 15 days (120 hours) per year
3-5 years of service: 20 days (160 hours) per year
6-10 years of service: 25 days (200 hours) per year
10+ years of service: 30 days (240 hours) per year
PTO accrues on a per-pay-period basis. Employees may carry over a maximum
of 40 hours of unused PTO to the following calendar year. Any PTO balance
exceeding 40 hours on December 31 will be forfeited.
3.2 Sick Leave
Employees accrue sick leave at a rate of one hour for every 30 hours worked,
up to a maximum of 48 hours per year. Sick leave may be used for the
employee's own illness, medical appointments, or to care for an immediate

up to a maximum of 48 hours per year. Sick leave may be used for the
employee's own illness, medical appointments, or to care for an immediate
family member. Unused sick leave carries over year to year, with a maximum
accrual cap of 120 hours.
3.3 Family and Medical Leave

Eligible employees may take up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per
year under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) for qualifying reasons
including: birth or adoption of a child, serious health condition of the
employee, or caring for an immediate family member with a serious health
condition. To be eligible, employees must have worked for the Company for at
least 12 months and have completed at least 1,250 hours of work in the
preceding 12 months.
3.4 Parental Leave
In addition to FMLA leave, the Company provides 8 weeks of paid parental
leave to all full-time employees following the birth, adoption, or foster
placement of a child. This benefit is available to both primary and secondary
caregivers and must be taken within 12 months of the qualifying event.
Page 3

SECTION 4: WORKPLACE CONDUCT AND STANDARDS
4.1 Professional Conduct
All employees are expected to conduct themselves professionally and treat
colleagues, clients, and business partners with respect. The Company maintains
a workplace free from harassment, discrimination, bullying, and intimidation.
Any behavior that violates this standard may result in disciplinary action up to
and including termination.
4.2 Attendance and Punctuality
Regular attendance is essential to the Company's operations. Employees are
expected to report to work on time and as scheduled. Unplanned absences
should be reported to the employee's supervisor as soon as possible, but no later
than 30 minutes after the scheduled start time. Excessive absenteeism or
tardiness may result in disciplinary action.

should be reported to the employee's supervisor as soon as possible, but no later
than 30 minutes after the scheduled start time. Excessive absenteeism or
tardiness may result in disciplinary action.
4.3 Remote Work Policy
Eligible employees may work remotely up to 3 days per week with supervisor
approval. Remote work arrangements require a signed Remote Work
Agreement and completion of a home office safety checklist. Employees must
maintain a dedicated workspace, reliable internet connection, and remain
accessible during core business hours (9:00 AM - 3:00 PM local time).

Data Security Reminder: Remote employees must comply with all
information security policies. Company data must not be accessed on
public WiFi networks without VPN. Confidential documents must not be
printed at home without secure disposal capability.
4.4 Dress Code
The Company maintains a business casual dress code. Employees should dress
appropriately for their work environment and any scheduled meetings or client
interactions. Client-facing roles may require business professional attire.
Specific department guidelines may apply.
Page 4

SECTION 5: INFORMATION SECURITY AND
CONFIDENTIALITY
5.1 Confidential Information
Employees may have access to confidential and proprietary information during
their employment. This includes but is not limited to: customer data, financial
information, trade secrets, business strategies, product plans, and employee
information. Employees must not disclose confidential information to
unauthorized persons during or after employment.
5.2 Data Protection Requirements
1. All company devices must use full-disk encryption and require password
authentication.
2. Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include uppercase, lowercase,
numbers, and symbols.
3. Multi-factor authentication is required for all company systems and
applications.

2. Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include uppercase, lowercase,
numbers, and symbols.
3. Multi-factor authentication is required for all company systems and
applications.
4. Customer personal data must be handled in accordance with applicable
privacy laws including GDPR and CCPA.
5. Data breaches or suspected security incidents must be reported to IT Security
within 1 hour of discovery.

5.3 Acceptable Use of Technology
Company technology resources including computers, email, internet access,
and software are provided for business purposes. Limited personal use is
permitted provided it does not interfere with job responsibilities, violate any
policy, or create security risks. Employees should have no expectation of
privacy when using Company systems.
Prohibited activities include: downloading unauthorized software, accessing
inappropriate websites, sharing login credentials, connecting personal devices
to the corporate network without approval, and using company email for
personal business ventures.
5.4 Social Media Guidelines
Employees who use social media must not disclose confidential company
information, speak on behalf of the Company without authorization, or engage

5.4 Social Media Guidelines
Employees who use social media must not disclose confidential company
information, speak on behalf of the Company without authorization, or engage
in conduct that reflects poorly on the Company. When discussing work-related
matters, employees should clearly state that views expressed are their own and
not those of the Company.
Page 5

SECTION 6: DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES AND
TERMINATION
6.1 Progressive Discipline
The Company generally follows a progressive discipline approach, though the
Company reserves the right to skip steps or proceed directly to termination
depending on the severity of the violation. Progressive discipline typically
includes:
1. Verbal Warning: Documented conversation addressing the performance or
conduct issue.
2. Written Warning: Formal written notice detailing the issue, expected
improvement, and consequences of continued violations.
3. Final Written Warning: Notice that further violations will result in
termination.
4. Termination: Separation of employment.
6.2 Immediate Termination Offenses
Certain conduct may result in immediate termination without progressive

termination.
4. Termination: Separation of employment.
6.2 Immediate Termination Offenses
Certain conduct may result in immediate termination without progressive
discipline, including but not limited to:
Theft, fraud, or dishonesty

Violence, threats of violence, or possession of weapons on company
property
Harassment or discrimination
Unauthorized disclosure of confidential information
Working under the influence of drugs or alcohol
Falsification of company records or employment documents
Gross negligence resulting in significant harm to the Company
6.3 Resignation and Voluntary Termination
Employees who wish to resign are requested to provide at least two weeks'
written notice. Management and professional positions are requested to provide
four weeks' notice when possible. Upon separation, employees must return all
company property including laptops, access cards, keys, and documents.
6.4 Final Pay and Benefits
Final paychecks will be issued in accordance with applicable state law.

6.4 Final Pay and Benefits
Final paychecks will be issued in accordance with applicable state law.
Accrued, unused PTO will be paid out at the employee's regular rate of pay.
Information regarding COBRA continuation of health benefits will be provided
within 14 days of separation.

In my dream I stood in the great halls of Helios. Now you might be wondering how I knew
that, for the palace wasn’t golden, or adorned with images of a hot ball of gas that would
make someone want to fall to their knees and shout, ‘Praise the sun!’ In fact, the palace was
an oppressive, suffocating thing made of obsidian as black as night with no windows to speak
of. The air was so thick and cloying it was as if I was at the bottom of the ocean, or enduring
the kind of humid summer day that makes you really sit with the fact that billionaires are
destroying the planet just so they can fly private jets and buy their eighth yacht.

Circe knelt at her feet. “Grandmother. He will die.”
The Titaness—Thetis, I somehow knew—did not look up from her river-stone green yarn.
“Of course he will. He is a mortal, that is their lot.”
“It is not fair,” Circe sniffed. “It cannot be.”
“Those are two different things.”
Circe shook her head. “You must help me. Great goddess, will you not take him to your halls
and make him eternal?”
“No god can do so much.”
“But I love him,” Circe said. “Glaucos is different.”

Circe shook her head. “You must help me. Great goddess, will you not take him to your halls
and make him eternal?”
“No god can do so much.”
“But I love him,” Circe said. “Glaucos is different.” 
“Real,” I murmured under my breath. Then I shook my head; in the past, Circe had been able
to interact with me when I dreamed of her. “You can’t save him. Choose the bear, girl!”
But Circe ignored me. “There must be a way,” she implored her grandmother.
Thetis sighed. “Do you know how many nymphs before you have hoped the same and been
disappointed?” 
“Is there not some—I do not know the word. Some bargain with the Fates, some trick, some
pharmaka—”
The sea snake around Thetis’s neck uncoiled and flicked a black tongue out. “You dare speak
of that?” she hissed, low and angry.

Circe’s face was wide with shock. “Speak of what?”
Thetis rose to her full height. “Child, I have done as much for you as may be done, and there
is no more. Go from here, and let me never hear you speak of that wickedness again.”
Circe’s face twisted in defeat, and then the scene changed into a blistering bright and sunny
day. “Jesus—motherfuck, Circe, have some pity on a mortal!” I cried as I blinked bright spots
away from my vision.
She ignored me, for she was too busy ogling the mortal standing opposite her as if he had
hung the moon. Or should I say the sun?
Sorry.
Anyway, it was midday and hot, the soil beneath our feet dry and cracked. “Come,” Circe
said. “A perfect sleeping spot to ease your weary bones.”

Circe shook herself out of her thoughts, her smile still soft and innocent. “Do you mean
Scylla?”
“Yes, Scylla,” Glaucos said. “She moves like water, does she not? Silver as a flowing
stream.”
“Oh, you sweet summer child,” I whispered to myself.

heavily, like his mouth had gone bone-dry. “I can’t do it anymore.”

Annabeth’s eyebrows had risen the longer he spoke. “What are you trying to say?” she asked,
slow and delicate.
“Run away with me,” he said. “It’ll be like the old days. We can find Thalia, and we’ll help
Grover find Pan, just like we always said we would. The Titans and the gods can fight this
war without us. What have they ever done for us?”
For a single moment, I saw Annabeth seriously consider Luke’s proposal. This idealized
future as selfish as a billionaire’s doomsday bunker and unrealistic as the sixth sequel to an
action movie. It only lasted a breath before it closed off. Not hardened, just… Dimmed. I was
seized with a sudden confidence that we both realized what Luke would see if he ever visited
the Sirens, and what it meant: 
Luke didn’t know how to build. He ran.

Circe’s Island, why didn’t you tell us?”
She glared at me with red and running eyes. I didn't know how to respond right away; we had
already talked about why I hid my magic from everyone last winter, hadn't we? But then I
thought about the last few months. Things hadn't been bad between Annabeth and I,
necessarily, but something had definitely shifted.  I guess neither of us wanted to address the
distance that had formed between us. It reminded me of the first summer we met, when
Annabeth thought I might be the traitor. 
With that thought in mind, I spoke honestly. “You guys were all terrified of magic. You made
it sound like Circe liking you was a death sentence. Annabeth, why should I have told you?”
“Because we’re your friends, you idiot!”

turning on a movie, and Annabeth made popcorn, so we sat for a while munching on Orville
Redenbacher’s and watching 10 Things I Hate About You.

particularly deep in the trenches of a thought spiral. Which, while concerning, was so
positively Annabeth-coded that I decided was a good thing.
“What did he mean, ‘a stepping stone?” she asked.
On screen, Kat Dennings was reading Sylvia Plath. I nodded in approval before I turned to
Annabeth. “I don’t know,” I replied, like a liar. “What do you think it means?”

Chiron. If Kronos has something planned… We’re running out of time.”

she was torn about saying something. I had a sneaking suspicion I knew what it was, and
after a few minutes of indecision I was proven correct. “There’s something I have to tell
you.”

“What?!” Percy and Rachel exclaimed in unison.
We got shushed again. I flipped the bird at the boy who had spoken. “Stop being thirsty,
Brad!”
Before he could retort, Rachel stood up and grabbed me by the wrist. I winced in pain, which
made her narrow her eyes, but Percy was standing with us. “What is it?” he asked.
“Later,” Rachel and I said in unison.
I offered apologies to the kids we stepped on as we hurried down the row and to the band
room. “Did they follow you?” Rachel asked as she dug through the instruments.
Percy looked back and forth between us. “Are you talking about those cheerleaders? I
thought you said you knew Tammi, Phoebe.”
I held out my hands. “So, about that—”
Rachel glared at me from behind Percy’s back.

Percy swallowed and glanced at me. “Me and Phoebe are half-bloods,” he said. “We’re half
human.”
“And half what?”
“Half that bitch,” I muttered under my breath right as the doors burst open. 
Tammi and Kelli stepped into the room. “There you are, Percy Jackson,” said Tammi. “It’s
time for your orientation!”
“We already know my brother is straight,” I huffed. “So you two can go now.”
“Not yet, Phoebe,” Tammi replied. “We’ve wanted to meet your brother for a long time now.”
Percy looked like he had just been sucker-punched, or like he had just torched the bowl of a
bong and was trying not to throw up all over himself. “What do they really look like?” he
said in a strangled tone. Needless to say, it did not help him beat the greening out allegations.

“I’ve got it,” I said before they could start bickering loud enough for everyone in a three

offended. “She’s coming with us.”
“She is?” I asked at the same time Rachel asked, “I am?”

Annabeth rolled her eyes. “Can you not sense it, Phoebe?”
“Um,” I replied intelligently. “Sense what?”
Annabeth rolled her eyes. “Rachel is a demigod. We can’t leave her behind.”
She marched off to call a taxi before we could react. Percy offered Rachel and I one
confused, conflicted, look, then he hurried after Annabeth. Once they were out of earshot,
Rachel and I stared at one another. “What the fuck?” I asked.
Rachel nodded sagely. “What the fuck,” she agreed. 
There really wasn’t much more we could say about it than that.

Foolishly, I thought the worst car ride of my life would be our road trip up to Maine. If only I
had known then how much worse it could get. 
Rachel was smart enough to call shotgun, and spent most of the drive chatting amiably with
the cabby. Every few miles she would meet my eyes in the rearview mirror, alternating
between the WHAT THE FUCK IS GOING ON face and sticking her tongue out at my
misfortune.
Annabeth was practically glued to the window. Percy twitched, bounced, and squirmed
beside me. Because yes, chat, I sacrificed my mental and emotional well-being and took the
middle seat. “How have you been?” he hazarded over me.
Annabeth grunted. 
“Have you heard anything about Nico?” 
“No.”

“This is really bad,” I said as soon as we were alone. 
Rachel pursed her lips, but to my surprise, she didn’t respond. 
I sat down in the tall grass. “You’re sure you weren’t secretly—”
“No.” Rachel jerked her head back and forth. “I was mortal. I am.”
“But then how—”
“I don’t know.” Rachel collapsed beside me and put her head in her hands. “Phoebe. What
the fuck is going on?”
I threw my hands into the air. “How am I supposed to know?”
“I don’t know!” 
We stewed in silence, leaving the other to their thoughts. Rachel had a habit of chewing her
lip and running her fingers along her jeans, which were stained with flecks of paint and what
looked like glitter. It was easy to imagine her taking a brush to the faded denim when she was
anxious.

you were.”
“Don’t say it—”
“Infatuated with my dear brother. And you’ll be a demigod. With me. Which is…” My eyes
widened. “Rachel… You don’t think you’re… You know…”

Rachel did wind up punching me that time.

“But you’re gay,” I said stupidly as we waited for Quintus to announce the games.
“There are gay people in Texas.” Lee glanced at Will, who was whispering with Jenny about
English Girl.
I rolled my eyes. “You know what I mean.”
“Unlike you, Sunshine, I can be discreet.”
I stuck my tongue out at him right as Quintus banged the pommel of his dagger against the
head table. “Right,” he said, standing up. In the torchlight, his gray hair made him look like a
ghost. “Gather round, everyone.”
“The flesh reflects the madness within,” I whispered.
Lee shot me an unimpressed, but still amused, look. 
“You will be in teams of two,” Quintus announced. Everybody obviously started talking and
trying to grab their friends. “Which have already been chosen!” he shouted over the din.

“About what?” Though his voice remained pleasant, Lee’s dark eyes roamed the foliage
constantly.
“Hmm, I don’t know, what could I be talking about?”
He sighed. “Phoebe, you know that doesn’t narrow it down. The Great Prophecy? You being

“I—you know that?”
“Dad.”
“Oh that bitch.”
“Eh, it was pretty obvious. You think Dad would pop out a kid that emo?”
“Gerard Way—”

I really had to hand it to Rachel. It turned out there was a time and place for subtlety. 
In this case, it meant ‘accidentally’ bumping into Lee when he drew an arrow to defend
Annabeth and Percy from what I was mentally calling blast-ended skrewts. That half-second
was all it took for Percy’s butt to collide with Annabeth and she fell into the gap between the
rocks. She grabbed Percy like a kitten, fingers scrunching the back of his collar and dragging
him in after her. The last we heard was his strangled yelp before they vanished into thin air.
Or so it would have looked to Lee. To me, it was…
Um…
Different. 
Very different.
“It eats people?” I whispered.
Lee stared at me. “What eats people?”
“Oh, gods, Annabeth doesn’t know the half of it,” I whispered to myself. “That means—”

locked on where Silena and I held hands atop the ping pong table. I was about to raise my
eyebrow in confusion when realization hit me like a bucket of cold water, again. 
Look, it was hard to remember that Silena, the girl who had helped me prepare for my first
quest, who taught me how to do my makeup and braid my hair, who snuck out to the city
with me on the weekends to laugh at the boys… That my friend was a spy for Kronos. 
Or maybe I just didn’t want to believe it. Not even when I knew with absolute certainty that it
was true.

“Carol—!”
Rachel ignored me and collapsed at the center table. She plopped her feet onto the worn
wood and laced her fingers behind her head. I wanted to live out my Charlie Day dreams, but
ultimately we didn’t have that much time.  
I’m not sure how long we went over everything. We started by double-checking the original
timeline, then the potential off-shoots Bianca’s presence might cause. If you’ve seen the Loki
TV show, it was sort of like how the TVA tracks Nexus Events. Each branch was denoted
with a different string, with blue being the best case scenario and black being the ‘Please Say
This Is Like Edge of Tomorrow’ scenario. Once we had everything squared away, we turned
to the more immediate problems.

Sometimes Rachel got like this. Now that I knew both of them personally, I understood why
Percy developed a crush on Rachel. I’ve already mentioned how similar they were, but I
really felt it then. Just like Annabeth, Rachel was curious, opinionated, not afraid to call
Percy (or anybody) an idiot, and had a strong sense of morality and loyalty. Their differences
were subtle; where Annabeth wore her pride on her cheek, Rachel kept hers hidden. And
although the daughter of a billionaire was somehow less presumptuous at times (see Rules 5
and 6), she was far more entitled. It wasn’t something she did intentionally; remember, this
was the girl who spent all her free time attending protests and rallies for the good of
humanity and all that.

“I mean—” I stumbled, trying to justify something I had never really addressed before. In the
end, I gestured at all of our work sprawled out on the walls. “We did all of this so we could
stick as close to canon as possible so we can take down Kronos without all of our friends
dying! If we want to stay as close to canon as possible, then all we need to do is be on hand
to save her before she—”
“What?” Rachel was, in a word, flustered. “You don’t want to change anything?”
“What? No, that’s exactly what I’m trying to do—” 
“Phoebe, seventeen campers die because of Silena’s actions.” Rachel met my gaze stonily.
“Fourteen in the Battle of Manhattan. One in the sinking of the Andromeda. And two in the
Battle of the Labyrinth.”

“Yeah.” The words came out strangely garbled, and I had to clear my throat. “I mean, yeah.

knowing I wasn't going to be pleased. "What this prophecy means."
I looked away. "Let's start with Nico. He'll be at Triple-G Ranch, which should make things

“How?”
“Rachel, he’s like, ten years old. We can just take him.”
“You can’t just abduct a child, Phoebe.”
“I can if it saves him from Kronos!”
Rachel gave me a look that felt like she was hitting me over the head with the book on
avoidance.
“Alright, alright.” I slumped in my chair. “We could IM Bianca once we get there. If she and
Thalia showed up…”
“That’s assuming Nico wants to see his sister.”

“What? Reminding you of your sunshine personality?”
“My personality is not—wait.” 
“What?”
“Oh, fuck,” I breathed. “Rachel, do I get energy from the sun? Do I need to
photosynthesize?” 
Rachel eyed me critically. “I mean, it might make you more powerful—”
“Fuck fuck fuck fuck fuck! Rachel, I’m cooked!” I let out a wail and reached for her. 
“What? Phoebe, what’s wrong?”
“The sun! Without it… I’ll die!” I gasped. 
“Phoebe, what are you talking about?”
I sat up with a shudder. “When Will went to the Underworld and Tartarus he said the lack of
sunlight nearly killed him. Now, that could be because he’s the most perfect angel ever and
his powers are more related to the sun than me—"

desert. But you came back to us then, didn’t you?”

Then the wall exploded (take that, Nostalgia Critic!). 
Tourists screamed. I squinted my eyes so I could ‘see double’ and saw the monster as the
mortals did. Which is to say, she transformed into a rogue construction crane, which I had to
admit was really fucking funny. Maybe I shouldn’t have laughed, though, because Briares
briefly looked like he was going to throw me at the monster and make a bid for the sea.
In reality, Kampê held two swords: long bronze scimitars that glowed with a greenish aura,
boiling wisps of vapor that smelled sour and hot like a nuclear caramel apple. “Poison!”
Grover yelped. “Don’t let those things touch you or…”
“You’ll die?” Percy guessed.
“After you shrivel slowly to dust, yes,” Grover replied.
“Let’s avoid the swords.”

Tyson ripped a metal lamppost out of the ground. “I will distract Kampê. You run around,
back to the prison.”
“I’ll help you,” Percy declared.
“No,” Tyson argued. “Go. Poison will hurt cyclopses. A lot of pain. But it won’t kill.”
Percy didn’t look happy. “Are you sure?”
Tyson nodded. “Go. I will meet brother and sister inside.”
It was really fucking cute. I was so proud of him! Which meant that, unfortunately, I had to
lie to him. With everyone distracted by the most terrifying monster imaginable, I focused on
the mist swirling around us. It was the first time I planned on manipulating the Mist since I
had—Fuck, since I had totally fucked with Paul’s mind! Gods fucking damn it, this was
becoming a Harry Potter fanfic, wasn’t it?

chest, succeeding in making her stagger backwards, but already the wound around her middle
was closing to reveal a snarling dog.

“Look for the mark!” Annabeth barked.
We did, and soon Grover found the Delta etched into the back of the prison cell. The stone
wall opened slowly. Too slowly. Kampê was barreling towards us, swords flashing as
dangerously as her eyes. Percy pushed Briares, Tyson, Annabeth, and Grover into the maze. I
beat him to it, though, and shoved him through the opening.
“Phoebe—!” 
“Bang!” I screamed as I leapt backwards into the Labyrinth, both guns pointed out like I was
Star Lord from Infinity War giving Thanos a double bird.

Slowly, I took stock of our surroundings. We were in a room full of waterfalls. Beneath our
feet water rushed through a complicated path that emptied into a black hole, sort of like an
open manhole on the street. But regular manholes didn’t breathe in with evil intent. 
“Tartarus,” I whispered hoarsely.
Briares nodded. “Yes. I should jump in and save everyone the trouble.”
I didn’t join the Briares pity party. Not that anyone’s words worked; the moment he brought
up his ‘faded’ brothers I knew there was no way he was going to listen to us. Percy marched
after him when he left, leaving Tyson curled up in a large ball beside one of the waterfalls.
Annabeth’s eyes were glued on the entrance to Tartarus.
Enough with the foreshadowing, jeez, I thought to the Fates.

Annabeth looked away from the pit and at me. “How were you able to do that?” she asked
quietly.
“Do what?”
She gave me that perfected You’re being an idiot look. 
“Oh, the clone? I—Well… Um…” I scratched the back of my head. How did I do that? It
wasn’t something I had ever attempted before. “I wanted to help Tyson, and it was the only
way I could think of.”
Annabeth’s expression, if possible, grew even more scornful. “You mean you didn’t know
what you were doing.”
“Yeah, hasn’t that been pretty obvious?”
“Then what did that book teach you?” Grover asked. 
I scowled. “That magic is all about vibes.”
“You mean you weren’t joking.” Annabeth was now openly glaring. “All this time, you’ve
just been, what? Goofing around?”

After a little while we settled on a corridor made of huge marble blocks. It looked like it

Annabeth decided it was a good sign.
“We must be close to Daedalus’s workshop,” she said. “Get some rest. I’ll take first watch.”
She didn’t need to look at me to know that I was also on first watch. I kept my back to the

Grover was out like a light. Tyson was not. He tinkered with some metal scraps from his
building kit for a while, but he kept disassembling the pieces with a frown. His eye was
bloodshot from crying.

He heaved a big sad sigh, then closed his eye. The metal pieces fell out of his hands, still
unassembled, and he began to snore. I found myself looking back and forth between Percy’s
shield, which because of my actions was no longer melted into goo, and the holsters at my
side. Last summer I tried to befriend Tyson so he could make me cool weapons at the forges.
Only now I had yet to ask him for anything. I only had to wonder why for a moment when an
image of Beckendorf, smirking as he showed off the insane ammo types he and Jake had
cooked up, sprang to mind.
Maybe I had been bracing myself for the deaths of my friends. Maybe I was just eager to
have something to remember them by. Only now that they weren’t certain… I didn’t know.

Maybe I had been bracing myself for the deaths of my friends. Maybe I was just eager to
have something to remember them by. Only now that they weren’t certain… I didn’t know.
So much of canon had stayed the same. Which was what I wanted, wasn’t it? The closer to
canon we were, the easier it was to predict what would happen next. Easier to try to save
them. Something about the idea made my chest tighten. Rachel’s face floated in my mind’s
eye, reminding me that everything had already changed.
I shoved the reminder away. I didn’t need to have a panic attack while we were in the
Labyrinth. 
Percy eventually stood up, stretched, and sat on the wall opposite me and beside Annabeth.
“You should sleep,” she said, trying hard to sound stern and utterly failing.

“No we didn’t. Your plan worked perfectly.”
Annabeth smiled softly. “I guess. Remember when Phoebe asked Hades not to eat her?”
“Don’t remind me,” I sighed.

In my dream I stood on a boat bobbing in the gentle waters of a harbor. The docks were a
flurry of activity; fishermen, soldiers, and other men wearing garb I could best describe as
‘Ancient Greek coded’ shouted at one another and worked tirelessly, shielded from the sun by
the shadows of a great city that loomed in the hills above us. The buildings were made of
stone, weathered and worn but still somehow timeless. I could have believed I was looking at
the ruins of an Ancient Greek city if it were not so busy, if there was not so much color;
pillars and roofs were stained brilliant crimson, deep blue, gleaming gold… Bare-footed
children raced up and down every road and alleyway, their laughter nearly as loud as the men
working the docks.

in charge of dreams or whatever. And for as much as I thought Apollo was a loser, I didn’t
think he would make me watch the Minotaur’s birth if there wasn’t a point.

“Where is bad guy?”
“No bad guys,” I wheezed, dutifully looking at the ground. “Just cows. Normal cows.”
“They do not look like normal cows,” observed Tyson. 
“Because they’re not,” said Annabeth. “They’re red cattle. The cattle of the sun.”
“What?” Percy and I asked in unison.
Annabeth had the audacity to offer me a tentative grin. “They’re sacred to Apollo.”
“You mean—” Percy began.
“Don’t say it!” I tried.
“Holy cows?”
I shook my head with a grimace. “Terrible. Just terrible.”

“Don’t say it!” I tried.
“Holy cows?”
I shook my head with a grimace. “Terrible. Just terrible.”
While I was grateful to my brother for adding some levity to the situation, I was less pleased
when he, Annabeth, and Grover all started laughing at my reaction to the ‘holy cows.’
Because chat: the cows were obsessed with your girl. They meandered over to me, mooing in
a manner that should have been very cute, but I kept imagining a screaming little monster
with grubby baby hands and—
“Are you scared of cows?” asked Tyson seriously.
“Nope, not at all!” I said cheerfully. “Just—Allergic. Yeah, allergic. A–a–achoo!”
Grover lost it completely, falling onto Percy’s shoulder as his shoulders heaved with sobs.
“She’s scared of cows!”
“New Yorkers,” Annabeth sighed. “They aren’t going to bite you.”

I cackled like a maniac as I sprinted ahead, then spun around in a slow circle with my eyes
closed and my hands stretched out wide. “I’m just a girl who’s going to be okay,” I
whispered. “Gods, where can a bitch get a matcha latte around here?”
“You are okay?” Tyson called. Right, monster hearing.
“More than okay, buddy. Want to race?”
He scratched his head. “Not fair?”
“That’s what you think,” I retorted, and after confirming with a visibly nonplussed Eurytion
that the trail would lead us straight to Geryon’s ranch, we took off. Tyson handily destroyed
me, but I was just grateful to stretch my legs and get my blood moving. Plus, it got us fucking
away from the cows, which was really all I needed to feel better.

into the shadows at his feet. “Nico went bye!” Tyson called out helpfully.
I grimaced, my eyes narrowed. I wasn’t sure what I was looking for, exactly, but the more I
concentrated, the more I was able to glean. There was a pattern to the mist surrounding us:
Grover was surrounded by a dark, evergreen color like a spruce tree, while Tyson’s burned
red and hot. Annabeth was surrounded by a clump of gray and blue mist that swirled
chaotically around her, even more violent than the deep blues and greens that surged around
my brother like a violent tide.
Then the Mist cleared. Nico stood across the clearing from us, sword in hand and triumphant.

“All magic begins with desire, Phoebe. Why do you think we women are more oft blessed by
Hecate? Men are given everything on a silver platter. They grow lazy and fat and apathetic.
Women are denied. Most of our sisters are beaten down, molded in a forge to whatever shape
is expected of them. If they resist, they are broken beyond repair. We, Phoebe, are swords.
Forged in fire, sharpened with Magic…”
“But Circe could,” Ariadne said quietly, staring at where her hands were joined together in
her lap. Beside her mother, who glowed golden with divinity, she was just a girl. “Because
she understood what it is like to be mortal. To be like…” Her voice faded out, but her mother
understood her.

Percy shuddered. “Good luck.”
“You’re such a woke king,” I told him solemnly.
“Thought you’d be happy to hear that,” he said, and then he leaned over and mussed up my
hair! I couldn’t stop myself from giggling; despite Silena’s magic the Texas humidity had my
hair almost as unruly as Annabeth’s. She caught my eye with an expression I couldn’t read.
Then it shuttered, and she turned to Eurytion. “You won’t be helping Kronos’s army, then?”
“Shoot, no.” Eurytion spat so hard it flew all the way into the grass. Percy and Grover’s eyes
lit up in interest. “I reckon you’ll be looking for Daedalus’s workshop now?”
Now Annabeth was the intrigued one. “Can you help us?”
Eurytion shifted uncomfortably. “Don’t know where it is. But Hephaestus probably would.”

My questing companions and I (barring Tyson, was still going ham on the pancakes) shared a
dark look at the mention of Kronos. “Phoebe…” Annabeth started.
I looked away. “It was my fault.”
“That’s not what I was going to say,” Annabeth said at the same time Percy exclaimed, “No,
it wasn’t!”
I smiled at them both. “It was,” I repeated. “I should have noticed something was wrong.”
“I should have noticed the lack of monster dust,” said Annabeth.
“I should have felt the disturbance in the Wild,” said Grover.
Tyson burped. “I should not eat more.”
“Good call, man,” said Percy, and clapped him on the back. I smiled softly at the pair of
them, which Percy returned in kind. “Just because that demigod used magic, doesn’t mean it
was your fault.”

Oh, he was so blushing! I fought down a cackle as he shifted awkwardly and nodded to
Annabeth.

enough to see the moment Percy told Annabeth to leave him. She protested wildly, hair
bouncing erratically and arms flailing like two windmills. Opposite her Percy remained
resolute, like a sturdy rock beating against the current of the ocean.
Then Annabeth surged forward, kissed him, and put on her invisibility cap before I could
even blink.
"Gods damn it!" I screeched under my breath. I didn’t even have a moment to think about
reaching for my camera! The injustice of it all! At the very least I got to witness my brother
staring stupidly into the distance, punch-drunk on his crush, until the telekhines noticed him.

Then everything went wrong. 
With a great bark of surprise and pain one of the telekhines exploded into dust. Percy stared,
as absolutely shooketh as I was, when Annabeth materialized where the telekhine had just
stood, dagger in one hand and her Yankees cap in the other. “Percy!” she shouted.
I recovered a second after my brother, nocking an arrow and sending it flying towards the
pack of telekhines flopping down the bridge towards my brother and my best friend. And, for
a single moment, I thought we had a chance. Percy deflected a goopy handful of lava while
Annabeth rolled out of the way of a telekhine’s bite. I hit a young telekhine in the eye with an
arrow and it exploded over all its friends.

line of telekhines with a single slice, but it wouldn’t be enough. Annabeth collapsed on the

too far away, and he was on the same platform as her. What was I supposed to do? Conjure
up a big fireball and yell ‘Bang!’
Everything suddenly slowed. I could see what would happen clearly in my mind's eye. With
Annabeth injured, Percy would never use his powers to make the volcano erupt. He would
fight—valiantly, to be sure—but it wouldn't matter. He and Annabeth would die. 
All while I sat on the ledge of the volcano with a bow in hand, and did nothing. 
Again.

What better described the space between than me? Both from this world, and not? Sally
Jackson’s daughter, Percy Jackson’s sister… But not. And if I thought all the way back to my
very first quest… When I met Morpheus, the god of dreams, who rules the domain between
sleeping and waking… What had he told me?

“You alone can walk the veil, which means you alone can pierce it.”
All this time I had been terrified of changing the ‘canon timeline.’ Even after I watched my
own mother die at the hands of the Minotaur. After I watched my brother get poisoned by
Luke. After I watched Reyna and Hylla get kidnapped, after I watched Annabeth hold up the
weight of the sky, after I watched Zoë die... Everything I had done had been in an effort to
keep things the same, afraid that if I interjected, I would make everything worse. I stood at
the back of fights, refused to use my magic unless I absolutely had to, all to make sure things
played out the way they were supposed to. I had denied myself, denied my power, so I
wouldn’t change anything drastically.

But that wasn't the truth, was it? No, I knew the real reason now. The horrible, selfish,
nauseating reason I had refused to see my real purpose here.
I didn't want blood on my hands. 
I wanted this—isekai, future memories, whatever you want to call it—to not matter. I wanted
to believe the Fates had willed the canon story to progress with or without me. If I saved the
lives of my friends that was all for the better, but if not... At least I could blame the Fates.
At least then I wouldn't have to blame myself.  
But where had that gotten me? Nico was fully in his alt-right era. Annabeth was on fire.

But where had that gotten me? Nico was fully in his alt-right era. Annabeth was on fire.
Rachel was a fucking demigod, which meant we had no clue who would guide us through the
Labyrinth, who would tell Percy he wasn’t the hero of the prophecy, and who would usher in

I guess the book on avoidance was actually a boomerang, and here it was coming around to
hit me in the face, all as I sat back and continued to do nothing. 
Hera was right. I always had access to the answer.
I had just been running away from it.

hit me in the face, all as I sat back and continued to do nothing. 
Hera was right. I always had access to the answer.
I had just been running away from it.
I stood up, my bow falling limply from my fingers. Later I would realize I dropped it right
into the pit of the volcano. I tried to remember the feeling of magic. The euphoric rush of it.
The thrum of it. The hum of it.
And there it was, waiting for me. Like it always had been, only I had been too scared to
acknowledge it.
Across the fiery pit of Mount St. Helens, Percy and I locked eyes. Even though it should have
been impossible, I knew what he was mouthing to me: Save her!
I didn’t hesitate. 
I thrust out a hand and allowed magic to flow through me. “ἐ μοί!” I commanded. To me!

It was like a hook wrapped around Annabeth’s middle and yanked her towards me. She flew
over the lava, shrieking all the while, fingers clenched around her dagger and her Yankees
cap. I concentrated, sweat beading my brow, as my brother burned. He stumbled onto one
knee, Riptide clattering onto the platform beside him. The telekhines surrounded him.
I caught Annabeth, hauled her over my shoulder, and took off for the entrance to the
Labyrinth. Just as we reached it I heard my brother scream, a terrifying bellow befitting a
god. 
I clenched my hand into a fist and the ceiling of the Labyrinth came crashing down behind us
in a pile of rock and dust as Mount St. Helens erupted.

Chapter End Notes
So... I have a lot of thoughts I want to share with you all!
One thing I've always hated is that Rick made Annabeth a little selfish in this book. In
canon, she does not support Grover running off to find Pan, and straight up ditches
Percy in the volcano. i only have one thing to say to that: fuck that shit! I've seen some
people who think that Annabeth and Percy's fatal flaws should be reversed, and while
I'm not totally sure about Percy, I do think Annabeth's loyalty isn't talked about enough.
I just can't see her abandoning Percy, or telling Grover to abandon his dreams.
As for the ending... This was a moment I have been trying to build toward for awhile :)
